solution: The denominators are equal, so subtract the numerators over the common denominator: $\frac{({=m}x+{=a})-({=n}x+{=b})}{x+{=p}}$.
Remove the brackets and collect like terms: $({=m}-{=n})x+({=a}-{=b})={=m-n}x+{=a-b}$.
The result is $\frac{{=m-n}x+{=a-b}}{x+{=p}}$; it cannot be simplified further, and the domain is $x\neq -{=p}$.

families.stem: Add and give the answer in simplest form: $\frac{{=a}}{x+{=p}}+\frac{{=b}}{x-{=q}}$ (the denominator may be left factorised).
solution: The denominators $x+{=p}$ and $x-{=q}$ have no common factor, so the L.C.M. is $(x+{=p})(x-{=q})$.
Rewrite each fraction over the L.C.M.: $\frac{{=a}(x-{=q})+{=b}(x+{=p})}{(x+{=p})(x-{=q})}$.
The result is $\frac{{=a+b}x+{=b*p-a*q}}{(x+{=p})(x-{=q})}$. The numerator has no factor in common with the denominator. The domain is $x\neq -{=p}$ and $x\neq {=q}$.
